question.:question/problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=4 y$ along the curve parametrized by $r(t)=\langle t^{2},t\rangle$ for $t\in [0,\sqrt{6}].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To calculate the line integral, we will use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $r(t)=(t^{2})\,i+(t)\,j$, then along the curve we have $x=t^{2}$, $y=t$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =(2 t)\,i+(1)\,j \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(2 t)^2+(1)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=4 y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(4)(t) \\  & =4 t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}(4 t)(\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 1})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=4 t^{2} + 1$, $\text{d}u=(8 t)\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}4 t \sqrt{4 t^{2} + 1}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{25}\frac{1}{2}\cdot u^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\big|_{1}^{25} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(25)^{3/2}-(1)^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(125)-(1)] \\  & =(\frac{125}{3})-(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{124}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=3 \cos{\left(x \right)}$ along the curve parametrized by $r(t)=\langle 2 t^{2},- 4 t^{2}\rangle$ for $t\in [0,\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To calculate the line integral, we will use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $r(t)=(2 t^{2})\,i+(- 4 t^{2})\,j$, then along the curve we have $x=2 t^{2}$, $y=- 4 t^{2}$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 4 t^{2})\,j \\  & =(4 t)\,i+(- 8 t)\,j \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(4 t)^2+(- 8 t)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{80 t^{2}} \\  & =4 \sqrt{5}|t| \\  & =4 \sqrt{5} t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $|t|=t$ because $t\geq0$ along the path of $C.$

Now, since $f(x,y)=3 \cos{\left(x \right)}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =3 \cos{\left(2 t^{2} \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}(3 \cos{\left(2 t^{2} \right)})(4 \sqrt{5} t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=2 t^{2}$, $\text{d}u=(4 t)\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{\sqrt{3} \sqrt{\pi}}{6}}12 \sqrt{5} t \cos{\left(2 t^{2} \right)}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}}3 \sqrt{5}\cdot \cos u\,\text{d}u \\  & =3 \sqrt{5}\sin u\big|_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} \\  & =3 \sqrt{5}[\sin(\frac{\pi}{6})-\sin(0)] \\  & =3 \sqrt{5}[(\frac{1}{2})-(0)] \\  & =(\frac{3 \sqrt{5}}{2})-(0) \\  & =\frac{3 \sqrt{5}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{3 y + 3 z}{x}$ along the curve parametrized by $r(t)=\langle t,t^{2},\frac{3 t^{2}}{2}\rangle$ for $t\in [1,\sqrt{2}].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To calculate the line integral, we will use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $r(t)=(t)\,i+(t^{2})\,j+(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})\,k$, then along the curve we have $x=t$, $y=t^{2}$, $z=\frac{3 t^{2}}{2}$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(3 t)\,k \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^2+(2 t)^2+(3 t)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{13 t^{2} + 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=\frac{3 y + 3 z}{x}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{(3)[(t^{2})+(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})]}{t} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{15}{2})t^2}{(1)t} \\  & =\frac{15 t}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}(\frac{15 t}{2})(\sqrt{13 t^{2} + 1})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=13 t^{2} + 1$, $\text{d}u=(26 t)\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{15 t \sqrt{13 t^{2} + 1}}{2}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{14}^{27}\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{15}{52}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{15}{52}{\int }_{14}^{27}u^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{15}{52}\cdot\frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\big|_{14}^{27} \\  & =\frac{5}{26}[(27)^{3/2}-(14)^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{5}{26}[(81 \sqrt{3})-(14 \sqrt{14})] \\  & =(\frac{405 \sqrt{3}}{26})-(\frac{35 \sqrt{14}}{13}) \\  & =- \frac{35 \sqrt{14}}{13} + \frac{405 \sqrt{3}}{26}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s=\int_a^b f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,k \\  & =(2)\,i+(3 t)\,j+(2 t)\,k \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})^2+(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^2+(3 t)^2+(2 t)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{13 t^{2} + 4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=\frac{4 y + 4 z}{x}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{(4)[(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})+(t^{2})]}{2 t} \\  & =\frac{(10)t^2}{(2)t} \\  & =5 t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}(5 t)(\sqrt{13 t^{2} + 4})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}5 t \sqrt{13 t^{2} + 4}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{30}^{56}\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{5}{26}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{26}{\int }_{30}^{56}u^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{26}\cdot\frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\big|_{30}^{56} \\  & =\frac{5}{39}[(56)^{3/2}-(30)^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{5}{39}[(112 \sqrt{14})-(30 \sqrt{30})] \\  & =(\frac{560 \sqrt{14}}{39})-(\frac{50 \sqrt{30}}{13}) \\  & =- \frac{50 \sqrt{30}}{13} + \frac{560 \sqrt{14}}{39}\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{(2)[(t^{2})+(\frac{3 t^{2}}{2})]}{2 t} \\  & =\frac{(5)t^2}{(2)t} \\  & =\frac{5 t}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}(\frac{5 t}{2})(\sqrt{13 t^{2} + 4})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=13 t^{2} + 4$, $\text{d}u=(26 t)\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{5 t \sqrt{13 t^{2} + 4}}{2}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{30}^{43}\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{5}{52}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{52}{\int }_{30}^{43}u^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{52}\cdot\frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}\big|_{30}^{43} \\  & =\frac{5}{78}[(43)^{3/2}-(30)^{3/2}] \\  & =\frac{5}{78}[(43 \sqrt{43})-(30 \sqrt{30})] \\  & =(\frac{215 \sqrt{43}}{78})-(\frac{25 \sqrt{30}}{13}) \\  & =- \frac{25 \sqrt{30}}{13} + \frac{215 \sqrt{43}}{78}\end{aligned}
$$
